analysis: Reviewed the base text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-797). Per file_changes, the PR only modifies the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a documentation section about an excluded startup shape warmup (head lines ~956-986); no code or configuration changes are in this batch. The added warmup text describes ordinary EngineV2 slots running a greedy 128-token probe twice plus solo and served-width shape cells under a 20-second budget. It states that no probe or cell trains a rate or counter, and that the warmup runs before registration so routed traffic cannot preempt it. Relevant threat IDs: T-029 (resource availability), T-028 and T-041 (cache/GPU residual data and the TTFT oracle), A-001. The text implies the warmup uses synthetic prompts and the artifact's default sampling, so it does not add consumer-data exposure. It does not claim prefix-cache population from warmup, and the SSD cache gating, TTL and HMAC claims in T-041 are unaffected. The visible base text makes no change to the T-041 cache posture. Remaining integration questions, which I could not verify because the patch excerpt is truncated and the implementation is not supplied: (1) whether warmup prompts could donate to the SSD prefix cache or the coordinator's cache-evidence/epoch, which would be a synthetic-prefix and timing-signal concern; (2) whether warmup memory is reserved through the shared KV budget; (3) whether a request arriving before registration is handled safely for the local endpoint, which the docs say can preempt the warmup. These are documentation claims, not verified code behavior. No security regression is identified from the doc-only change.
